full_judgment: 3. Mr. Rafiqur Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing in support of the Rule bas contended that the learned Magistrate has found at page 10 of his judgment, that there is a bonfire dispute regarding the title of the tank, The lower appellate Court has assumed that the Municipality had been in possession of the tank according to the lower appellate Court otherwise for taking lease the complainant would not spend money for paying the 'salami'. In my opinion this approach to the case in wrong. It is for the prosecution to prove that they bad given possession to the lessee which they had on the basis of which they had in some right the tank. There is nothing in the evidence of the witnesses for the prosecution to show that the Municipality was the owner of the tank P. W. 5 who is an Overseer of the Municipality has said nothing about the ownership of the Municipality over the tank. He has in cross-examination after recall admitted that the record-of-rights stands in the name of Rahman Chand Bibi, the wife of accused Chand Mia. The blower appellate Court has held that from the plot number given in the S. A. Khattan the identity of the tank cannot be established with the identity of the tank purchased by the wife of the petitioner Chand Mia. The C. S  Khatian exhibited on behalf of the petitioner’s shows the Khatian number of the plot in question is 368 and the Plot No. is 2137. The deed exhibit A also shows the same. The admission of P. W. 5 and the deed led the taught Magistrate to hold that there was a bonfire dispute regarding the title of tale tank in question. That being the position it is difficult to accept the finding of the lower appellate Court. As I have already stated the lower Appellate Court moved from the premises that because the complainant has spent money. Therefore, the possession must have been given to him the Municipality after the lease. There is no evidence to show that the Municipality was in possession of the tank in question except the evidence of P. W. 3 and P. W. 5 who in cross examination admitted that the record of right of the tank is in the name of the petitioner Chand Mia. The evidence, therefore, that the complainant is in possession is based on no document of possession or title of the Municipality from whom he got his possession. The lessee must prove that the lessor had the right to grant lease and to deliver possession. That has not been done in this particular case, P. W. 5 has also admitted that there is nothing in writing to show that he was asked by the Municipality to deliver possession to the complainant.
